title: Editing Tips — Audio + MIDI
intro: The tricks in this section work identically on audio regions and MIDI regions. Learn them once and you have doubled their value.

tips.t: ⌘T splits every selected region at the playhead
tips.d: Select multiple regions across multiple tracks and one keystroke cuts them all at the same point. This is how you chop a whole arrangement in one move.
Works on audio and MIDI. On audio it creates a new merged file; on MIDI it merges the events into a single region.

tips.t: ⌥‑drag copies, ⌥⇧‑drag makes an alias or clone
tips.d: The single most useful modifier in the program, and it behaves consistently everywhere.
For a numeric count, use Edit > Repeat Multiple… and type the number.

tips.t: Trim to the playhead from either direction
tips.d: The commands are “Trim Region Start to Playhead” and the matching End command — search them in Key Commands and put them on keys. No mouse precision needed.

tips.t: Use the length fields in the Region inspector
tips.d: Position, length and loop status are all typeable. When precision matters, stop dragging and start typing.

tips.t: Set Snap to Smart and leave it there
tips.d: Smart snap adapts to your zoom level, so you get bar accuracy zoomed out and tick accuracy zoomed in, automatically.

tips.t: Two modifiers, two grades of precision
tips.d: Hold ⌃ while dragging for a finer snap division, and ⌃⇧ for tick-level free movement. Release and normal snap comes back.

tips.t: Turn on “Snap Regions to Absolute Value”
tips.d: In the Snap menu. Regions snap to the grid itself rather than preserving their offset from it. Turn it on for tidy work, off when you are moving a region that is deliberately off‑grid.
Set the nudge value in Edit > Move, then ⌥← and ⌥→ move anything by exactly that value, every time.

tips.t: Esc opens the tool menu, Esc twice returns to the pointer
tips.d: Fastest tool switching in the program. Numbers 1–9 pick tools directly from the menu.
Hold ⌘ to temporarily switch to your assigned secondary tool. It is Marquee by default, which is exactly right.

tips.t: Assign the Fade tool to ⌘ when doing audio cleanup
tips.d: Set the secondary tool via the right‑hand tool menu, then every ⌘‑drag across a region edge creates a fade.

tips.t: Select everything after this point in one keystroke
tips.d: ⇧F is Select All Following: it grabs every region after the current selection, across all tracks — the fastest way to shift a whole song later. To stay on one track, use Edit > Select > All Following of Same Track; it ships with no default key, so give it one in Key Commands.

tips.t: Select equal or similar regions in one command
tips.d: Edit > Select > Similar Regions (⇧S), Equal Regions, or Equal Colored Regions finds all matching regions across the project instantly.

tips.t: Lock a region so you cannot move it by accident
tips.d: Control-click the region and choose Lock SMPTE Position, or use the track's protect padlock — it is hidden by default, so turn it on via the track header configuration.
